title: Prakrama 1, Sarga 5. The Appearance of Sri Chaitanya
html:
Shachi bears in her womb a portion of Hari; the hymn of the gods to Shachi; the Lord's birth on the full-moon night of Phalguna during a lunar eclipse; the prediction of Nilambara Chakravarti; the rites after the birth

Verse 1

शृणुष्वावहितं ब्रह्मन्चैतन्यस्यावतारकम्।
नवीनं जगदीशस्य करुणावारिधेर्विभोः॥१॥

śṛṇuṣvāvahitaṁ brahmancaitanyasyāvatārakam|
navīnaṁ jagadīśasya karuṇāvāridhervibhoḥ||1||

shrinushva — hear; avahitam — attentively; brahman — O brahmana; chaitanyasya — of Chaitanya; avatarakam — (the account of) the descent; navinam — new; jagad-ishasya — of the Lord of the world; karuna-varidheh — the ocean of compassion; vibhoh — the all-powerful.

1"Hear attentively, O brahmana, the new story of the descent of Chaitanya — the all-powerful Lord of the world, the ocean of compassion.

Verse 2

गते देवर्षिवर्ये तु स्वाश्रमे भगवान्परः।
जगन्नाथस्य विप्रर्षेर्मनस्याविशदच्युतः॥२॥

gate devarṣivarye tu svāśrame bhagavānparaḥ|
jagannāthasya viprarṣermanasyāviśadacyutaḥ||2||

gate — when had gone; devarshi-varye — the best of divine sages (Narada); tu — and; sva-ashrame — to his own hermitage; bhagavan — Bhagavan; parah — the Supreme; jagannathasya — of Jagannatha; vipra-rsheh — the brahmana sage; manasi — into the mind; avishat — entered; achyutah — Achyuta (the Infallible).

2When the best of the divine sages1 had gone to his own hermitage, the Supreme Bhagavan Achyuta entered the mind of Jagannatha, the brahmana sage.

Verse 3

तेनाहितं महत्तेजो दधार समये सती।
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे साध्वी शची पतिपरायणा॥३॥

tenāhitaṁ mahattejo dadhāra samaye satī|
etasminnantare sādhvī śacī patiparāyaṇā||3||

tena — by him (Jagannatha); ahitam — placed; mahat — great; tejah — splendour; dadhara — received; samaye — in due time; sati — the chaste one; etasmin antare — meanwhile; sadhvi — the virtuous; shachi — Shachi; pati-parayana — devoted to her husband.

3In due time the chaste wife received the great splendour he had placed in her. Thus the virtuous Shachi, devoted to her husband,

Verse 4

लेभे गर्भं हरेरंशं गङ्गेव शाम्भवं शुभा।
तस्यास्तेजोऽतिववृधे शुक्लपक्षे यथा शशी॥४॥

lebhe garbhaṁ hareraṁśaṁ gaṅgeva śāmbhavaṁ śubhā|
tasyāstejo'tivavṛdhe śuklapakṣe yathā śaśī||4||

lebhe — conceived; garbham — an embryo; hareh — of Hari; amsham — a portion; ganga — the Ganga; iva — like; shambhavam — (the seed) of Shambhu; shubha — the auspicious one; tasyah — her; tejah — splendour; ati-vavridhe — greatly increased; shukla-pakshe — in the bright fortnight; yatha — as; shashi — the moon.

4auspicious, conceived a child — a portion of Hari2 — as the Ganga once received the seed of Shambhu3; and her radiance waxed like the moon in the bright fortnight.

Verse 5

तां दृष्ट्वा रूपसम्पन्नां तप्तचामीकरप्रभाम्।
श्रिया युक्तो जगन्नाथो मुमुदे हृष्टमानसः॥५॥

tāṁ dṛṣṭvā rūpasampannāṁ taptacāmīkaraprabhām|
śriyā yukto jagannātho mumude hṛṣṭamānasaḥ||5||

tam — her; drishtva — seeing; rupa-sampannam — endowed with beauty; tapta-chamikara-prabham — shining like molten gold; shriya — with splendour (good fortune); yuktah — endowed; jagannathah — Jagannatha; mumude — rejoiced; hrishta-manasah — with a delighted heart.

5Seeing her beauty and her glow like molten gold, Jagannatha, graced with good fortune, rejoiced with all his heart.

Verse 6

अथ तां तादृशीं दृष्ट्वा देवा ब्रह्मादयोऽपरे।
गन्धर्वा अमरा ये च ये च सेन्द्रा नभोगताः॥६॥

atha tāṁ tādṛśīṁ dṛṣṭvā devā brahmādayo'pare|
gandharvā amarā ye ca ye ca sendrā nabhogatāḥ||6||

atha — then; tam — her; tadrishim — such; drishtva — seeing; devah — the gods; brahma-adayah — headed by Brahma; apare — others; gandharvah — the Gandharvas; amarah — the immortals; ye cha — and those who; ye cha — and those who; sa-indrah — together with Indra; nabhah-gatah — dwelling in the sky.

6Then, seeing her so, Brahma and the other gods, the Gandharvas, the immortals and the dwellers of the sky together with Indra

Verse 7

कृताञ्जलिपुटा हर्षात्साश्रुकण्ठविलोचनाः।
तुष्टुवुर्मुदिताः सर्वे प्रणामानतकन्धराः॥७॥

kṛtāñjalipuṭā harṣātsāśrukaṇṭhavilocanāḥ|
tuṣṭuvurmuditāḥ sarve praṇāmānatakandharāḥ||7||

krita-anjali-putah — with joined palms; harshat — out of joy; sa-ashru-kantha-vilochanah — with tears in their throats and eyes; tushtuvuh — praised; muditah — joyful; sarve — all; pranama-anata-kandharah — with necks bent in obeisance.

7joined their palms in joy; with tears in their voices and eyes, their heads bowed in obeisance, they all joyfully sang her praise:

Verse 8

नमामि त्वां सदागर्भामदितिं जननीं हरेः।
चन्द्रार्काग्निप्रभागर्भां सत्त्वगर्भां धृतिं क्षमाम्॥८॥

namāmi tvāṁ sadāgarbhāmaditiṁ jananīṁ hareḥ|
candrārkāgniprabhāgarbhāṁ sattvagarbhāṁ dhṛtiṁ kṣamām||8||

namami — I bow; tvam — to you; sada-garbham — ever bearing (Him) in the womb; aditim — Aditi; jananim — the mother; hareh — of Hari; chandra-arka-agni-prabha-garbham — bearing in the womb the radiance of moon, sun and fire; sattva-garbham — bearing pure being (sattva) in the womb; dhritim — steadfastness; kshamam — forbearance (the earth).

8'We bow to you who ever bear Him in your womb! You are Aditi, the mother of Hari; you bear in your womb the radiance of moon, sun and fire, you bear pure being in your womb; you are steadfastness and forbearance;

Verse 9

अद्वेषगर्भां संसिद्धिं वेदगर्भां स्वयं हरेः।
देवकीं रोहिणीं चैव यशोदां सर्वथाभवाम्॥९॥

adveṣagarbhāṁ saṁsiddhiṁ vedagarbhāṁ svayaṁ hareḥ|
devakīṁ rohiṇīṁ caiva yaśodāṁ sarvathābhavām||9||

advesha-garbham — bearing freedom from malice in the womb; samsiddhim — perfection; veda-garbham — bearing the Veda in the womb; svayam — himself; hareh — of Hari; devakim — Devaki; rohinim — Rohini; cha eva — and also; yashodam — Yashoda; sarvatha-bhavam — the source (of being) in every way.

9you bear freedom from malice in your womb; you are perfection; you bear in your womb the Veda — Hari Himself. You are Devaki, Rohini and Yashoda — in every guise the source of being4.

Verse 10

तं वै बिभर्षि गर्भे त्वं यो यज्ञं प्रथयिष्यति।
कीर्तनाख्यं महापुण्यं यद्यज्ञैर्नोपपद्यते॥१०॥

taṁ vai bibharṣi garbhe tvaṁ yo yajñaṁ prathayiṣyati|
kīrtanākhyaṁ mahāpuṇyaṁ yadyajñairnopapadyate||10||

tam — him; vai — indeed; bibharshi — you bear; garbhe — in the womb; tvam — you; yah — who; yajnam — the sacrifice; prathayishyati — will spread; kirtana-akhyam — called kirtana; maha-punyam — supremely holy; yat — which; yajnaih — by (ordinary) sacrifices; na upapadyate — is not attained.

10You bear in your womb Him who will spread the holiest of sacrifices — kirtana, whose fruit no (ordinary) sacrifice can attain.

Verse 11

कीर्तनं नृहरेः श्रुत्वा निमिषार्धेन या भवेत्।
प्रीतिरस्मादृशां सा तु कोटियज्ञैर्भवेन्न हि॥११॥

kīrtanaṁ nṛhareḥ śrutvā nimiṣārdhena yā bhavet|
prītirasmādṛśāṁ sā tu koṭiyajñairbhavenna hi||11||

kirtanam — the glorification; nrihareh — of Nrihari; shrutva — hearing; nimisha-ardhena — in half a moment; ya — which; bhavet — arises; pritih — joy; asmadrisham — for such as us; sa — that; tu — indeed; koti-yajnaih — by millions of sacrifices; bhavet — would arise; na hi — not at all.

11Not even millions of sacrifices could give the joy that arises in such as us from half a moment of hearing the kirtana of Nrihari.

Verse 12

अहो महत्पुरा दत्तममृतं हरिणा स्वयम्।
समुद्रमन्थनं कृत्वा ततः कोटिगुणाधिकम्॥१२॥

aho mahatpurā dattamamṛtaṁ hariṇā svayam|
samudramanthanaṁ kṛtvā tataḥ koṭiguṇādhikam||12||

aho — oh; mahat — great; pura — once; dattam — given; amritam — the nectar of immortality; harina — by Hari; svayam — himself; samudra-manthanam — the churning of the ocean; kritva — having performed; tatah — than that; koti-guna-adhikam — millions of times greater.

12Oh! Great was the nectar of immortality that Hari Himself once gave after churning the ocean5 — yet a sweetness a million times greater

Verse 13

रसं पश्याम एवात्र शृण्वन्तः श्रीहरेर्यशः।
मोक्षमप्यनृतं चेतो मन्यते कीर्तनाद्धरेः॥१३॥

rasaṁ paśyāma evātra śṛṇvantaḥ śrīhareryaśaḥ|
mokṣamapyanṛtaṁ ceto manyate kīrtanāddhareḥ||13||

rasam — a sweetness (rasa); pashyamah — we behold (taste); eva — indeed; atra — here; shrinvantah — hearing; shri-hareh — of Sri Hari; yashah — the glory; moksham — liberation; api — even; anritam — false (worthless); chetah — the mind; manyate — considers; kirtanat — because of the kirtana; hareh — of Hari.

13we taste here, hearing the glory of Sri Hari: for the sake of the kirtana of Hari the mind counts even liberation as nothing.'

Verse 14

एवमुक्त्वा ततो देवाः सेन्द्रा जग्मुः प्रणम्य ताम्।
ब्रह्माणमग्रतः कृत्वा गायन्तः श्रीहरेर्यशः॥१४॥

evamuktvā tato devāḥ sendrā jagmuḥ praṇamya tām|
brahmāṇamagrataḥ kṛtvā gāyantaḥ śrīhareryaśaḥ||14||

evam — thus; uktva — having spoken; tatah — then; devah — the gods; sa-indrah — with Indra; jagmuh — went away; pranamya — bowing; tam — to her; brahmanam — Brahma; agratah — in front; kritva — placing; gayantah — singing; shri-hareh — of Sri Hari; yashah — the glory.

14Having spoken thus, the gods with Indra bowed to her and, placing Brahma at their head, departed, singing the glory of Sri Hari,

Verse 15

स्वां पुरीं श्रीपतेरंशो जातो भुव्यतिहर्षिताः।
कलेर्भाग्यं प्रशंसन्तो नृत्यन्तः प्रेमविह्वलाः॥१५॥

svāṁ purīṁ śrīpateraṁśo jāto bhuvyatiharṣitāḥ|
kalerbhāgyaṁ praśaṁsanto nṛtyantaḥ premavihvalāḥ||15||

svam — to their own; purim — city; shri-pateh — of the Lord of Shri; amshah — a portion; jatah — is born; bhuvi — on earth; ati-harshitah — (saying this) overjoyed; kaleh — of Kali; bhagyam — the good fortune; prashamsantah — praising; nrityantah — dancing; prema-vihvalah — overwhelmed with love.

15to their own city. Overjoyed that a portion of the Lord of Shri had been born on earth, they praised the good fortune of (the age of) Kali and danced, overwhelmed with love.

Verse 16

ततः पूर्णे निशानाथे निशीथे फाल्गुने शुभे।
काले सर्वगुणोत्कर्षे शुद्धगन्धवहान्विते॥१६॥

tataḥ pūrṇe niśānāthe niśīthe phālgune śubhe|
kāle sarvaguṇotkarṣe śuddhagandhavahānvite||16||

tatah — then; purne — when was full; nisha-nathe — the lord of the night (the moon); nishithe — at midnight; phalgune — in (the month of) Phalguna; shubhe — auspicious; kale — at a time; sarva-guna-utkarshe — excellent in every quality; shuddha-gandha-vaha-anvite — filled with a pure breeze.

16And then at midnight, in the auspicious month of Phalguna, when the moon, the lord of the night, was full, at an hour rich in every excellence and fanned by a pure breeze,

Verse 17

मनःसु देवसाधूनां प्रसन्नेषु च शीतले।
स्वर्नद्याः शुद्धसलिले जाते जातः स्वयं हरिः॥१७॥

manaḥsu devasādhūnāṁ prasanneṣu ca śītale|
svarnadyāḥ śuddhasalile jāte jātaḥ svayaṁ hariḥ||17||

manahsu — when the minds; deva-sadhunam — of gods and saints; prasanneshu — were serene; cha — and; shitale — cool; svar-nadyah — of the heavenly river (Ganga); shuddha-salile — when the water had become pure; jate — had become; jatah — was born; svayam — himself; harih — Hari.

17when the minds of the gods and the saints were serene and the waters of the heavenly river cool and pure — Hari Himself was born.

Verse 18

तं विकाशिकमलेक्षणं लसत्पूर्णचन्द्रवदनं कनकाभम्।
तेजसा वितिमिरा दिशः स्वयं कारयन्तमुपलभ्य सुतं सः॥१८॥

taṁ vikāśikamalekṣaṇaṁ lasatpūrṇacandravadanaṁ kanakābham|
tejasā vitimirā diśaḥ svayaṁ kārayantamupalabhya sutaṁ saḥ||18||

tam — him; vikashi-kamala-ikshanam — with eyes like blossoming lotuses; lasat-purna-chandra-vadanam — with a face like the shining full moon; kanaka-abham — golden; tejasa — by his splendour; vitimirah — free of darkness; dishah — the quarters; svayam — himself; karayantam — making; upalabhya — having obtained; sutam — the son; sah — he.

18The son he had obtained was golden; His eyes were like blossoming lotuses, His face like the shining full moon, and by His own splendour He drove the darkness from every quarter.

Verse 19

प्रीतिसागररसस्य न पारं प्राप पद्मनिधिना यथाऽधनः।
श्रीजगन्नाथमिश्रपुरन्दरः प्रेमगद्गदमुखं सदा दधे॥१९॥

prītisāgararasasya na pāraṁ prāpa padmanidhinā yathā'dhanaḥ|
śrījagannāthamiśrapurandaraḥ premagadgadamukhaṁ sadā dadhe||19||

priti-sagara-rasasya — of the waters of the ocean of joy; na — not; param — the further shore; prapa — reached; padma-nidhina — (on gaining) the padma treasure; yatha — as; adhanah — a poor man; shri-jagannatha-mishra-purandarah — Sri Jagannatha Mishra Purandara; prema-gadgada-mukham — a mouth faltering with love; sada — constantly; dadhe — had.

19And Sri Jagannatha Mishra Purandara, like a poor man who has found the padma treasure6, could not reach the further shore of his ocean of joy, and his voice kept faltering with love.

Verse 20

तस्य जन्मसमयेऽनु शशाङ्कं राहुरग्रसदलं त्रपयेव।
कृष्णपद्मवदनेन निर्जितः प्राविशत्सुररिपोर्मुखं विधुः॥२०॥

tasya janmasamaye'nu śaśāṅkaṁ rāhuragrasadalaṁ trapayeva|
kṛṣṇapadmavadanena nirjitaḥ prāviśatsuraripormukhaṁ vidhuḥ||20||

tasya — his; janma-samaye — at the time of birth; anu — then; shashankam — the moon; rahuh — Rahu; agrasat — swallowed; alam — completely; trapaya — out of shame; iva — as if; krishna-padma-vadanena — by the lotus face of Krishna; nirjitah — defeated; pravishat — entered; sura-ripoh — of the enemy of the gods; mukham — the mouth; vidhuh — the moon.

20At the hour of His birth Rahu swallowed the moon entirely: defeated by the lotus face of Krishna, the moon, as if out of shame, hid in the mouth of the enemy of the gods7.

Verse 21

तत्र पुण्यसमये मनुजानां कीर्तनं नरहरेः कृतं जनैः।
पूजनं सपदि जाह्नवीजले स्नानदानमघमार्जनं शुचौ॥२१॥

tatra puṇyasamaye manujānāṁ kīrtanaṁ narahareḥ kṛtaṁ janaiḥ|
pūjanaṁ sapadi jāhnavījale snānadānamaghamārjanaṁ śucau||21||

tatra — at that; punya-samaye — holy time; manujanam — by men; kirtanam — the kirtana; narahareh — of Narahari; kritam — was performed; janaih — by the people; pujanam — worship; sapadi — at once; jahnavi-jale — in the waters of the Jahnavi; snana-danam — bathing and giving of gifts; agha-marjanam — cleansing from sin; shuchau — in purity.

21At that holy hour the people sang the kirtana of Narahari and offered worship, and then, keeping themselves pure, they bathed in the waters of the Jahnavi, gave gifts and performed the rite of cleansing from sin.

Verse 22

जहृषुः सुरगणाः समहेन्द्राः पद्मसम्भवमहेशपुरोगाः।
अप्सरोभिरतिनृत्यपराभिर्नायकाश्च सुमनांसि ववर्षुः॥२२॥

jahṛṣuḥ suragaṇāḥ samahendrāḥ padmasambhavamaheśapurogāḥ|
apsarobhiratinṛtyaparābhirnāyakāśca sumanāṁsi vavarṣuḥ||22||

jahrishuh — rejoiced; sura-ganah — the hosts of gods; sa-mahendrah — with Mahendra; padma-sambhava-mahesha-purogah — led by the Lotus-born (Brahma) and Mahesha; apsarobhih — with the apsaras; ati-nritya-parabhih — absorbed in dancing; nayakah — the leaders (of the Gandharvas); cha — and; sumanamsi — flowers; vavarshuh — rained down.

22The hosts of gods rejoiced together with Mahendra, with the Lotus-born and Mahesha at their head; the apsaras gave themselves to dancing, and the leaders (of the Gandharvas) rained down flowers.

Verse 23

नीलाम्बरचक्रवर्ती जन्मना तस्य हर्षितः।
आजगामाश्रमं तूर्णं जामातुः सर्वशास्त्रवित्॥२३॥

nīlāmbaracakravartī janmanā tasya harṣitaḥ|
ājagāmāśramaṁ tūrṇaṁ jāmātuḥ sarvaśāstravit||23||

nilambara-chakravarti — Nilambara Chakravarti; janmana — by the birth; tasya — of him; harshitah — delighted; ajagama — came; ashramam — to the home; turnam — quickly; jamatuh — of his son-in-law; sarva-shastra-vit — knower of all scriptures.

23Delighted by His birth, Nilambara Chakravarti, the knower of all scriptures, hurried to the home of his son-in-law.

Verse 24

जगन्नाथं समाहूय शचीं सम्बोधयन्सुधीः।
दौहित्रजन्मकालज्ञ इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥२४॥

jagannāthaṁ samāhūya śacīṁ sambodhayansudhīḥ|
dauhitrajanmakālajña idaṁ vacanamabravīt||24||

jagannatham — Jagannatha; samahuya — calling; shachim — Shachi; sambodhayan — addressing; sudhih — the wise man; dauhitra-janma-kala-jnah — knowing the time of his grandson's birth; idam — these; vachanam — words; abravit — spoke.

24The wise man, who knew (from the stars) the hour of his grandson's birth, called Jagannatha and, addressing Shachi, spoke these words:

Verse 25

अये पुरुषसिंहोऽयं जातः प्रोच्चे बृहस्पतौ।
असौ सर्वस्य लोकस्य पाता नित्यं भविष्यति॥२५॥

aye puruṣasiṁho'yaṁ jātaḥ procce bṛhaspatau|
asau sarvasya lokasya pātā nityaṁ bhaviṣyati||25||

aye — oh; purusha-simhah — a lion among men; ayam — this; jatah — is born; procche — when in exaltation; brihaspatau — Brihaspati (Jupiter); asau — he; sarvasya — of all; lokasya — the world; pata — the protector; nityam — always; bhavishyati — will be.

25'Oh! This lion among men is born when Brihaspati (Jupiter) stands in exaltation8. He will be the eternal protector of the whole world;

Verse 26

सुशीलः सर्वधर्माणामाश्रयो न्यासिनां वरः।
प्रीतिदः सर्वभूतानां पूर्णामृतकरो यथा॥२६॥

suśīlaḥ sarvadharmāṇāmāśrayo nyāsināṁ varaḥ|
prītidaḥ sarvabhūtānāṁ pūrṇāmṛtakaro yathā||26||

sushilah — of good character; sarva-dharmanam — of all dharmas; ashrayah — the refuge; nyasinam — of renunciants (sannyasis); varah — the best; priti-dah — giving joy; sarva-bhutanam — to all beings; purna-amrita-karah — the full moon (whose rays are nectar); yatha — like.

26of noble character, the refuge of all dharmas, the best of sannyasis, He will gladden all beings like the full moon pouring nectar.

Verse 27

समुद्धर्ता सदैवायं पितृमातृकुलद्वयम्।
एवमुक्ते द्विजे तस्मिन्सर्वे प्रमुदिता जनाः॥२७॥

samuddhartā sadaivāyaṁ pitṛmātṛkuladvayam|
evamukte dvije tasminsarve pramuditā janāḥ||27||

samuddharta — the deliverer; sada — always; eva — indeed; ayam — he; pitri-matri-kula-dvayam — of both lineages, father's and mother's; evam — thus; ukte — when had spoken; dvije — the brahmana; tasmin — that; sarve — all; pramuditah — rejoiced; janah — the people.

27He will forever deliver both lineages — His father's and His mother's.' When the brahmana had spoken thus, all the people rejoiced.

Verse 28

माता हर्षमतीवाप श्रुत्वा तत्पितृभाषितम्।
वात्स्यश्चकार पुत्रस्य जातकर्ममहोत्सवम्॥२८॥

mātā harṣamatīvāpa śrutvā tatpitṛbhāṣitam|
vātsyaścakāra putrasya jātakarmamahotsavam||28||

mata — the mother; harsham — joy; ativa — great; apa — obtained; shrutva — hearing; tat — that; pitri-bhashitam — speech of her father; vatsyah — the Vatsya (Jagannatha Mishra); chakara — performed; putrasya — of the son; jatakarma-maha-utsavam — the great festival of the birth rite (jatakarma).

28Hearing these words of her father, the mother was filled with great joy, and the Vatsya9 held a great festival — the jatakarma, the birth rite of his son.

Verse 29

ताम्बूलं चन्दनं माल्यं गन्धं प्रादाद्द्विजातये।
क्रमेणोत्थानकर्मादिमङ्गलानि चकार सः॥२९॥

tāmbūlaṁ candanaṁ mālyaṁ gandhaṁ prādāddvijātaye|
krameṇotthānakarmādimaṅgalāni cakāra saḥ||29||

tambulam — betel; chandanam — sandal paste; malyam — garlands; gandham — fragrances; pradat — gave; dvijataye — to the twice-born; kramena — in due order; utthana-karma-adi-mangalani — the auspicious rites beginning with the rite of rising (after childbirth); chakara — performed; sah — he.

29He gave the brahmanas betel, sandal paste, garlands and fragrances, and in due order performed the auspicious rites beginning with the utthana, the rite of "rising"10."

Thus ends the fifth sarga, "The Appearance of Sri Chaitanya" (Sri Chaitanya-avirbhava), of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Narada, at whose entreaty the Lord agreed to descend (Sarga 1.03).
  2. "Portion" (amsha; also in v. 15) does not mean that the Lord appeared only in part: in v. 17 Murari says plainly that "Hari Himself was born." Nor is this an ordinary conception: just as, according to the Bhagavata Purana (10.2.16–18), the Lord entered the mind of Vasudeva and through him Devaki, so here Achyuta entered the mind of Jagannatha (v. 2), and Shachi received his splendour.
  3. An allusion to the birth of Skanda: the seed of Shiva (Shambhu) was received by the Ganga.
  4. The reading of the last word of the verse is uncertain; the translation is tentative.
  5. The churning of the Milk Ocean by the gods and asuras, from which the nectar of immortality (amrita) was obtained.
  6. Padma is one of the nine treasures (nidhi) of Kubera.
  7. The Lord's birth coincided with a lunar eclipse; Rahu is the demon, "the enemy of the gods," who swallows the moon.
  8. The "exalted position" (uccha) of a planet in astrology is the sign of its greatest strength.
  9. The Vatsya is Jagannatha Mishra, of the Vatsya clan.
  10. Probably the rite marking the end of the lying-in period; another understanding is possible — the child's first standing up.
